title: It's My Life
trivia: The song opens with a talk-box guitar from Richie Sambora and was co-written with Swedish pop hitmaker Max Martin. It gave the band a fresh generation of fans fifteen years into their career.
notes: Single May 2000, album Crush Jun 2000.

title: Oops!... I Did It Again
trivia: The video, set on Mars with Spears in a red catsuit, became one of the defining pop images of 2000. The spoken-word bridge was as imitated as the chorus.
notes: Single Mar 2000, album May 2000.

title: One More Time
trivia: The processed vocals are by Chicago house singer Romanthony. The video is part of an anime film directed by Leiji Matsumoto and built around the duo's album.
notes: Single Nov 2000, album Discovery Mar 2001. Single-first year; Hitster NL also lists 2000.

title: Lady (Hear Me Tonight)
trivia: The groove is built on a looped guitar lick from a Chic track of 1982. It topped the charts across Europe in the summer of 2000.
notes: First released in France in 2000; album Modjo followed in 2001. Radio edit ~3:58, album/extended version ~5:08.

title: It Wasn't Me
trivia: Shaggy and singer RikRok play a man caught cheating and the friend who advises him to deny everything. It was never planned as a single, yet it became Shaggy's first US number one.
notes: Album Hot Shot Aug 2000; radio single Nov 2000, retail Feb 2001. Hitster NL credits Shaggy alone.

title: Fallin'
trivia: Keys wrote it and played the piano on it herself. It won the Grammy for Song of the Year in 2002.
notes: Single Apr 2001, album Jun 2001.

title: How You Remind Me
trivia: The Canadian band's breakthrough, it was Billboard's top single of 2002. A driving riff and a sullen vocal carried it around the world.
notes: Single Aug 2001, album Sept 2001.

title: Murder on the Dancefloor
trivia: It found a huge new audience in 2023, when it featured in the closing scene of a film and returned to charts worldwide. In 2001 it had already reached number two in the UK.
notes: Album Sept 2001, single Dec 2001.

title: Have a Nice Day
trivia: The band comes from the Welsh village of Cwmaman, and this singalong was one of its biggest hits in 2001. It reached the UK top five.
notes: Album Apr 2001; single later in 2001. Exact single date not checked.

title: Lose Yourself
trivia: It won the Oscar for Best Original Song, the first rap track to do so. Eminem did not attend the ceremony.
notes: Single and soundtrack Oct 2002. Album version is about 5:26; the radio edit is shorter. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: The Ketchup Song (Aserejé)
trivia: The nonsense chorus is a Spanish-sounding spoof of the opening lines of an early hip-hop hit. The song reached number one in many countries in 2002.
notes: Spanish single Jun 2002; album Jun 2002 in Spain.

title: Like a Prayer
trivia: A Eurodance remake of a Madonna hit, sung by Turkish singer Buse Ünlü. It topped the charts in Germany, Austria and Ireland.
notes: Cover of Madonna (1989); Hitster NL uses this recording. Group is a studio project listed as French, Dutch and Turkish. Single spring 2002, album Absolutely Mad 2002.

title: Dilemma
trivia: Destiny's Child member Kelly Rowland sings the hook. It spent ten weeks at number one in the US.
notes: Album Nellyville Jun 2002, single Jul 2002.

title: Feel
trivia: Williams wrote it with Guy Chambers, and the video features actress Daryl Hannah. It was one of the highlights of Escapology.
notes: Album Nov 2002, single Dec 2002.

title: In da Club
trivia: Dr. Dre and Mike Elizondo produced it, and it was the first number one for 50 Cent. The beat makes it an immediate floor-filler.
notes: Single Jan 2003, album Feb 2003.

title: Crazy in Love
trivia: It was her first solo single away from Destiny's Child. The brassy horn riff comes from a 1970 soul record.
notes: Single May 2003, album Jun 2003.

artist: Black Eyed Peas feat. Justin Timberlake
title: Where Is the Love?
trivia: A plea for tolerance and peace written in the aftermath of the early 2000s wars, with Justin Timberlake on the hook. It reached number one in the UK.

track.artist: Black Eyed Peas feat. Justin Timberlake
track.title: Where Is the Love?

notes: Single and album Jun 2003. Hitster NL credits the band alone.

title: Daughters
trivia: It won the 2005 Grammy for Song of the Year. The lyrics are about how fathers shape their daughters' ideas of love.
notes: Album Sept 2003, single Aug 2004. Album-first year; Hitster NL lists 2004. Hitster NL list shows 2004; card uses 2003.

title: Dragostea din tei
trivia: The Moldovan trio's Romanian-language hit was spread worldwide by the 2004 Numa Numa viral video. Its title translates roughly as love from the linden trees.
notes: Romanian single mid 2003; wider European release followed in 2004. Album DiscO-Zone date varies by source (Aug 2003 or Jun 2004). Single-first year 2003.

title: Hey Ya!
trivia: A line about shaking a Polaroid picture led Polaroid to issue a tongue-in-cheek statement that shaking is bad for the photo. André 3000 played most of the instruments.
notes: Single Sept 2003, album Sept 2003.

title: Mr. Brightside
trivia: Brandon Flowers wrote it after finding out about a girlfriend's cheating. It has since spent more weeks on the UK chart than any other song.
notes: Debut single released Sept 2003 (Lizard King), became a hit on re-release in 2004; Hot Fuss followed Jun 2004. Same studio recording. Hitster NL lists 2003. Not on the Hitster NL list; seen on the Hitster Canada edition list.

title: Seven Nation Army
trivia: The riff is played on a guitar run through an octave pedal, which makes it sound like a bass. Fans took it up as a stadium chant.
notes: Single Feb 2003, album Apr 2003. Not seen on any consulted Hitster edition list (NL, DE, FR, CA, Nordics); added for recognisability and decade balance.

title: Lonely
trivia: The hook leans on a 1960s hit about a lonely soldier. It was one of the breakout singles for the Senegalese-American artist.
notes: Album Trouble Jun 2004; single released later (UK 2005). Album-first year.

title: Call on Me
trivia: The Swedish producer built it on a sample of a 1982 song by Steve Winwood. The 1980s aerobics-class video became as famous as the track.
notes: Single Sept 2004 (T56, Data). No album. Radio edit is about 2:57 with the original mix ~7:34; the common version is a roughly 3 to 4 minute edit.

title: Numb/Encore
trivia: A mashup made for an MTV special that combined a Linkin Park track with a Jay-Z track. It won a Grammy for Best Rap/Sung Collaboration.
notes: Mashup of Linkin Park Numb (2003) and Jay-Z Encore (2003). Collision Course Nov 2004.

title: Because of You
trivia: Clarkson co-wrote it, and the lyrics draw on her parents' divorce. It was a follow-up to a string of big hits from the same album.
notes: Album Breakaway Nov 2004, single Nov 2005. Album-first year; Hitster NL lists 2005. Hitster NL list shows 2005; card uses 2004.

title: Yeah!
trivia: Lil Jon produced it, and it spent twelve weeks at number one in the US. The crunk beat and Usher's confident delivery made it the song of early 2004.
notes: Single Jan 2004, album Mar 2004.

title: Gold Digger
trivia: The hook sample comes from a Ray Charles hit. Jamie Foxx, who had just won an Oscar for playing Charles, sings the hook in Charles's style.
notes: Single Jul 2005, album Aug 2005.

title: Rehab
trivia: It was inspired by her refusing treatment for her drinking. It won the Grammys for Record of the Year and Song of the Year.
notes: Single Oct 2006, album Oct 2006.

title: World, Hold On (Children of the Sky)
trivia: Steve Edwards sings the soaring hook. The track topped the US dance club chart in summer 2006.

track.title: World, Hold On (Children of the Sky)

notes: Album Western Dream Apr 10 2006, single Apr 17 2006. Radio edit used for the duration.

title: Put Your Records On
trivia: The Leeds-born singer's debut album went straight to number one in the UK. This single is its sunny, laid-back calling card.
notes: Single Jan 2006, album Feb 2006.

title: No One
trivia: Co-written with Kerry Brothers Jr. and George Harry, it won the 2008 Grammy for Best Female R&B Vocal Performance. It is built around a gospel-tinged piano figure.
notes: Single Sept 2007, album Nov 2007.

title: This Is the Life
trivia: The Scottish singer-songwriter was only 19 when the album came out. The song did far better on the European continent than in her native UK.
notes: Album 30 Jul 2007; UK single Dec 2007; most of Europe 2008. Album-first year; Hitster NL lists 2007.

title: Do You Know? (The Ping Pong Song)
trivia: A table-tennis rally is the metaphor for a relationship going back and forth. A Spanish-language twin version, Dímelo, came out alongside.

track.title: Do You Know? (The Ping Pong Song)

notes: Single Apr 2007, album Insomniac Jun 2007.

title: Valerie
trivia: Originally by Liverpool band The Zutons. Ronson's brass-heavy cover, sung by Winehouse, is the version most people know.

track.title: Valerie
track.notes: Ronson and Winehouse version, not The Zutons.

notes: Cover of The Zutons (2006), but Ronson and Winehouse's is the famous recording. Version album 2007, single Sept 2007.

title: Relax, Take It Easy
trivia: The Beirut-born singer's soaring falsetto made the song stand out, and it was among his earliest releases. It reached the UK top 20 on its official release.
notes: Album Feb 2007; official UK single Dec 2007. A limited 7-inch pressing in Oct 2006 reportedly preceded both; card uses 2007, matching Hitster NL and the widely cited release.

title: Umbrella
trivia: It spent ten weeks at number one in the UK. The track was reportedly offered to other singers before Rihanna recorded it.
notes: Single Mar 2007, album Jun 2007. Not on the Hitster NL list; seen on the Hitster Canada edition list.

title: Viva la Vida
trivia: The title is Spanish for long live life and comes from a Frida Kahlo painting. Strings and a thumping marching beat replaced the band's usual guitar sound.

track.title: Viva la Vida
track.album: Viva la Vida or Death and All His Friends

notes: Single May 2008, album Jun 2008. Not on the Hitster NL list; seen on the Hitster Canada edition list.

title: Mercy
trivia: The Welsh singer's breakthrough single, it was a big European hit. It owes its sound to 1960s soul and girl-group records.
notes: Single Feb 2008, album Rockferry Mar 2008.

title: Poker Face
trivia: Gaga wrote it with producer RedOne, and it was her second US number one in a row. The song is about hiding what you really feel.
notes: Album Aug 2008, single Sept 2008. Album-first year (same year either way).

title: 4 Minutes
trivia: It gave Madonna her 37th top-ten hit on the US Hot 100, passing Elvis Presley's record. Timbaland produced it and Justin Timberlake features on the vocals.
notes: Single Mar 2008, album Apr 2008.

title: Whatcha Say
trivia: The hook leans on a sample of an Imogen Heap song. It was his debut single and went to number one in the US.
notes: Single May 2009, album Mar 2010. Single-first year.

title: Fireflies
trivia: Adam Young recorded it in his parents' basement in Owatonna, Minnesota. It topped the US Hot 100 in late 2009.
notes: Album Ocean Eyes Jul 2009.

title: Hey, Soul Sister
trivia: Frontman Pat Monahan co-wrote it with two Norwegian songwriters, Espen Lind and Amund Bjørklund. It became one of the biggest hits of 2009 and 2010.
notes: Single Aug 2009, album Oct 2009.
